You own track C of the "usable Android app" programme: displaying HTML mail. First read /home/exedev/email-os-usable/RULES.md in full and follow it. You are in phase 1: write ADR 0005 as a proposal, push it, report `ADR READY`, and stop. Do not implement until I send GREENLIGHT.

Today the reader is plain-text only on every platform (docs/current-status.md: "HTML mail rendering are not implemented"); most real mail is HTML, some with no text part. The reader must work in both the desktop layout and the phone (compact) layout, in the Tauri webview on macOS and Android, and in the browser preview.

The ADR must cover at least:
- Where the HTML comes from: what the Gmail sync stores today (bodies, MIME parts, size bounds, cache) and what must change in crates/mail-core to keep the HTML part; text/plain vs text/html choice and fallback when there is no text part.
- Safety: sanitising (in Rust or in the frontend; which library), isolation (sandboxed iframe with srcdoc, CSP, no scripts, no forms, no same-origin), and no access to Tauri IPC from mail content.
- Remote content: images and other remote resources blocked by default (tracking pixels), a per-message "load images" choice and whether it is remembered; `cid:` inline images from attachments.
- Links: they must go through the app's existing explicit link confirmation (links are disabled on Android today; say what HTML links do there and coordinate with track B, which owns the Android gates).
- Layout: fitting wide newsletters at phone width (scale vs reflow), dark mode, text size, quoted-text collapsing as today, selection/copy.
- Performance with large messages, and printing/forwarding are out of scope unless you argue otherwise.
- Fixture data: the synthetic provider needs HTML samples (newsletter, tracking pixel, cid image, malicious samples) so everything can be tested without real mail.
- Validation: tests for the sanitiser with hostile inputs, browser screenshots at desktop and phone width (light and dark), Android emulator screenshots.

Report back with `ADR READY: ...` and your open questions.

# Rules for the "usable Android app" tracks (read before you start)

Repository: Email OS (Tauri 2 + Vue 3 + TypeScript, Rust core in `crates/mail-core`, shell in `src-tauri`).
GitHub: `BbrSofiane/email-os`. A coordinator thread reviews your work; it talks to you through messages in your thread.

There are four tracks, each in its own worktree and branch from `origin/main`:

| Track | ADR number | Branch |
|---|---|---|
| A. Install and run (signing key, package, first-launch ANR, real devices) | 0003 | `usable/install` |
| B. Google sign-in on Android | 0004 | `usable/android-gmail` |
| C. HTML mail display | 0005 | `usable/html-reader` |
| D. Sending (macOS desktop and Android) | 0006 | `usable/send` |

Use only your own ADR number so the four files do not collide. Read the other tracks' rows so you know who owns what; if your design needs something from another track, write it under "Dependencies" in your ADR instead of building it yourself.

## Phase 1: ADR proposal (now)

1. Read `docs/current-status.md`, `docs/current-architecture.md`, `docs/development.md`, `docs/adr/0001-*.md`, `docs/adr/0002-*.md` and the code your area touches.
2. Write `docs/adr/000N-<short-slug>.md` (the number from the table). Match the tone of ADR 0002: plain, factual, no marketing. Status: `Proposed`. Sections:
   - **Context**: what exists today, with file:line references.
   - **Options considered**: at least two real options, with trade-offs.
   - **Decision** (proposed): the option you recommend, and why.
   - **Scope / out of scope.**
   - **Owner actions**: anything only the owner can do (Google Cloud console, GitHub secrets, a keystore password, a physical phone). Say exactly what and when it is needed. Never invent credentials, client IDs or keys.
   - **Dependencies** on other tracks, and what they need from you.
   - **Implementation plan**: ordered stages, each small enough for one sub-agent run, each with its own check (test, command or screenshot).
   - **Validation plan**: unit/integration tests, browser screenshots, Android emulator screenshots and screen recordings (videos) where the change is visible or a flow.
   - **Risks and open questions** for the owner.
3. Commit, push the branch (retry on transient remote errors), and end your turn with one line: `ADR READY: docs/adr/000N-....md @ <commit sha>`, followed by a short summary and your open questions.
4. Do **not** start implementing. No cargo or Android builds in this phase. Wait for a message from the coordinator: either review comments (revise, push, report `ADR READY` again) or `GREENLIGHT`.

## Phase 2: implementation (only after GREENLIGHT)

- Split the implementation plan into stages and hand each stage to a sub-agent with `delegate_task`: provider instance `codex`, model `gpt-6.1-terra`, option `reasoningEffort: high`, working in **your** worktree (no new checkout). Run stages one after another, not in parallel, in the same worktree. Give each sub-agent: these rules, the ADR, the exact stage, its check, and "commit when the check passes; do not push; no further delegation".
- After each stage, **review it yourself**: read the diff, run the stage's check, and fix or send it back. You own the result.
- When all stages pass: run the full gates (`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 mise run check:all`, plus the rendered tests below), do the validation plan (screenshots and videos), set the ADR status to `Accepted` with the decisions taken, update `docs/current-status.md` and `docs/development.md` where they change, push, and open a PR to `main`: `gh pr create -R BbrSofiane/email-os --base main`. The PR body lists what changed, the gates run with results, and the validation evidence (paths to screenshots/videos).
- End your turn with: `READY FOR REVIEW: <PR url> @ <head sha>` and the open items. The coordinator reviews and merges; you do not merge.

## Machine limits (shared by all tracks)

- 4 cores, 15 GB RAM, ~8 GB free disk. Only two tracks implement at the same time; the coordinator decides which.
- Rust: always `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`. One heavy command (cargo build/test, Android build, full test suite) at a time: before one, check `pgrep -fa 'cargo|gradle|vitest'`; if another track is building, wait and retry.
- Android build from a worktree: first `cp -n /home/exedev/email-os/src-tauri/gen/android/app/src/main/java/dev/exedev/emailos/androidfixture/generated/* src-tauri/gen/android/app/src/main/java/dev/exedev/emailos/androidfixture/generated/` (the shared target does not regenerate these), then `mise run android:build`.
- Do not create large files outside your worktree. Delete build outputs you no longer need.

## Android emulator (shared, one track at a time)

- Device host `local`, id `emulator-5554` (Android 15, x86_64, 1080×2400). Drive it with the T3 device tools (`device_open`, then the returned `agent-device` command; `device_screenshot`). `adb` only for install, logs and `run-as` file checks.
- Lock: before using it, create `/home/exedev/email-os-usable/emulator.lock` containing your branch name (`set -o noclobber; echo usable/xyz > …/emulator.lock`). If it exists and is not yours, wait. Remove it when done. Leave the app installed and the emulator as you found it (input method, airplane mode off).
- Before coordinate taps or `back`, confirm the app is in the foreground. Element refs (`@eN`) go stale after a screenshot: re-snapshot first.
- Screen recordings: `agent-device record` (see `help record`). Keep videos short (≤60 s).

## Validation evidence

- Browser screenshots: `EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME=/tmp/chrome-rendered/chrome/linux-156.0.8078.80/chrome-linux64/chrome EMAIL_OS_SCREENSHOT_DIR=<dir> mise run screenshots:mobile`. Rendered tests: `EMAIL_OS_RUN_RENDERED=1 EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME=<same chrome> pnpm vitest run --config vitest.config.ts <file>`.
- Put committed evidence under `docs/validation/<track-slug>/` (small PNGs; videos only if under ~5 MB, otherwise keep them in `/home/exedev/email-os-usable/<track-slug>/` and list the path in the PR).
- Synthetic data only in anything committed. Never commit real mail, tokens, client secrets, keystores or passwords. Never open any directory named `email-os-mobile-refs`.

## Working style

- Readable multi-line code that matches the surrounding style; no minified one-liners. Tests next to the existing ones.
- Product voice: terse and factual; never claim more than the app knows (pending, confirmed, failed and unknown stay distinct). No third-party brand names in UI copy.
- Do not use the repo's `implement` skill. Delegate only as described in phase 2.
- You run with full access. Never request escalated or sandbox-bypass permissions (nobody can approve them and you will stall). Keep temporary files inside your worktree (e.g. under `.git/`), not in `/tmp`. Pass PR bodies inline or from a file inside the worktree.
- If you are blocked on something only the owner can provide, say `BLOCKED:` with the exact need and stop; do not work around it with fake values.

# Current feature status

This page is the current feature inventory and validation summary. Slice and UX
contracts linked below define the detailed behavior and safety limits. Historical
research and architecture proposals are not feature inventories.

## Runtime availability

| Feature | Native fixture (default) | Explicit Gmail profile | Browser preview |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mailbox and reader | Durable synthetic inbox (the Gmail core on the built-in synthetic provider, [ADR 0002](adr/0002-fixture-as-synthetic-provider.md)), plain-text reader, read/unread mix, operation recovery. | Separate profile; bounded Gmail cache and plain-text reader. Read-only until the user enables mailbox actions. | Synthetic fixtures and in-memory state only; no Gmail, SQLite durability, or native IPC. |
| Mailbox writes | Archive/unarchive, read/unread and star/unstar (single and group), retry and undo, through the same operation ledger as Gmail; no permission grant. Interrupted writes are requeued at the next launch. | Explicit archive/unarchive, read/unread, and star/unstar setters only, after opt-in `gmail.modify` upgrade. No automatic read on open. | Fake-provider simulation only; does not prove provider writes or convergence. |
| Composition | Plain-text new message and reply; durable local drafts in the selected native profile. No send path. | Same local-only drafts; they do not sync to Gmail. No send path. | Synthetic drafts in memory; saves are not durable. |
| Search | Cached search over the 18 fixture conversations. | Read-only cached search or progressive provider scan, with bounded/incomplete coverage disclosures. | Synthetic fake search only. |
| Saved split | One local, account-scoped saved split. | One local split, removed on Gmail disconnect with cached account data. | Synthetic in-memory split. |
| Stars | Star/unstar setters and the cached Starred view, shown by the backend's `triageSurfaces` capability. | Starred cache browsing is read-only; explicit star/unstar setters require enabled Gmail modify capability. Cache coverage is incomplete. | Fake simulated-Gmail star state; not fixture-native or provider validation. |
| Reminders | Device-local reminders; schedule/reschedule/cancel/return do not write the provider. | Device-local reminders; schedule/reschedule/cancel/return do not write Gmail or require modify permission. | Synthetic in-memory reminder state. |
| Attachments and links | Synthetic fixture-text attachment listing/downloads. | Bounded cached descriptors and authenticated read-only Gmail fetch; explicit downloads create inert `.download` files. Links need explicit browser confirmation. No automatic opening or restricted document host. | Synthetic attachment surfaces only; no native download or Gmail fetch. |
| Multiple workspaces | One native session; native tabs are not implemented or certified. | One active Gmail profile/session. This is not real multi-account activation. | Two isolated synthetic in-app workspaces are supported by the preview. |

The Android fixture target builds a debug APK for ARM64 and x86_64 from the
shared Rust shell. It uses SQLite and the same synthetic fixture core as desktop
(ADR 0002); Gmail, attachment export, and external link dispatch are
unavailable. APK build passed on 2026-11-14. A pre-existing legacy fixture
database is retired once behind a startup screen. The unified-fixture APK was
smoke-tested on an Android 15 x86_64 emulator on 2026-11-15 (see below). Compact
phone layout is now in scope at widths ≤719px for Android fixture and browser preview.
The compact shell covers lists, reader, compose, search, reminders, utility pages,
contact details, command overlays and device-local swipe settings. Sending, reply-all,
forwarding, HTML bodies, label chips, multiple splits and destructive Trash/Spam/move
actions are not supported. Android uses fixture data; compact layout adds no mail IPC
or engine capabilities. See the
[Android smoke steps](development.md#android-fixture-apk).

The compact layout was checked on the same emulator on 2026-11-16 with a locally
built debug APK of the merged branch: swipe left to mark done and Undo, swipe
right to the reminder picker, long-press selection, the reader and its action
sheet, contact details, a new message typed with the software keyboard up, and
the saved draft in Drafts. Screenshots:
[inbox](<validation/mobile/android-inbox.png>),
[swipe and Undo](<validation/mobile/android-swipe-done-undo.png>),
[selection](<validation/mobile/android-selection.png>),
[drawer](<validation/mobile/android-drawer.png>),
[reader](<validation/mobile/android-reader.png>),
[reader actions](<validation/mobile/android-reader-more.png>),
[compose with keyboard](<validation/mobile/android-compose-keyboard.png>),
[drafts](<validation/mobile/android-drafts.png>),
[settings](<validation/mobile/android-settings.png>).
Known from that pass: the first launch right after a fresh install can still hit
the Android "isn't responding" dialog recorded for the original APK (a relaunch
is fine), and no physical device was used.

Mode selection is deliberate: native defaults to fixture; `EMAIL_OS_MODE=gmail`
selects a separate Gmail profile. Browser preview remains synthetic. See the
[development guide](development.md) for launch and validation commands.

Sending, provider-synced drafts, reply-all, Bcc, delete/Trash mutations, arbitrary
label editing, and HTML mail rendering are not implemented. Attachment saving
does not provide inline PDF/Office preview or malware scanning. External HTTP(S)
link dispatch is macOS-only; other platforms report it unavailable. See the
linked contracts for exact bounds and pending platform security gates.

## Validation status

The following is the baseline supplied for this documentation task at
`f361f57c4051c0af578af43277bed8170905548a`, not a rerun for this change:

| Check | Supplied result |
|---|---|
| `mise run check` | Passed: 315 Rust core tests; 1,162 frontend tests; 34 skipped. |

from those runtime gates. In particular, the baseline above does not certify

### Android unified-fixture smoke (2026-11-15)

Run on Android 15 (`t3-pixel`, x86_64 emulator) with the CI debug APK from the

The legacy-reset test used the CI APK from run 43645874365 (PR #63, head `63f7ab8`),

  reader stayed open on a neighbouring conversation rather than returning to the

  two seconds after Mark done, worked. This is the intended behaviour: Undo is
  available for 10 seconds after the action (`UNDO_WINDOW_SECONDS` in

Route: `adb install -r` of the main APK over the old one was refused with

**Not verified**

# ADR 0002: Fixture mode as a synthetic provider

**Status:** Implemented (stages 1–4). Stage 4 landed with the owner's decisions below: the default switched to the synthetic core, the legacy `MailCore` backend, its store and worker and the `EMAIL_OS_SYNTHETIC_CORE` opt-in were removed, and the one-time transition is the `fixture_transition` state machine behind the startup gate. The sections below are the original investigation and are kept as the record of why.

## Decisions

Taken on 2026-11-14 on the coordinating thread's recommendation, after the project owner asked for the remaining maintenance tickets to run. They authorise **stages 1 to 3** only. The owner can still redirect before stage 4 (switching the default and deleting the legacy backend); nothing below is a user-facing change until then.

1. **Staged unification**, as recommended above. The legacy `MailCore` backend stays the default and is not touched until stage 4.
2. **The unified fixture gains read and star.** Synthetic fixture mode admits archive, read and star (single and group), and the cached Starred list works. This departs from the "archive-only" wording in the stages and inventory below, which was about preserving today's errors. Cached Trash and provider destinations stay rejected with today's error variants. Connect, disconnect, permission upgrade and manual sync stay rejected with `InvalidRequest { field: "mode" }`, and nothing in synthetic mode may erase local state the way a Gmail disconnect does.
3. **Synthetic reminders follow the Gmail core's local rules** (hide locally, no provider write). The legacy fixture's archive/restore reminder phases are retired when stage 4 lands, not before.
4. **The on-disk transition (stage 4) is a one-time reset with disclosure and a retained backup**, local drafts untouched. It is planned, not implemented, in stages 1–3.

### Stage 4 decisions (owner, 2026-11-15)

5. **Interrupted writes are requeued by the synthetic policy.** A write interrupted before the provider recorded it is reconciled against the provider's durable facts at startup: landed means confirmed, unlanded means requeued and applied again. This matches the legacy fixture and is a session-policy method (`replay_unlanded_interrupted_writes`), not a mode check. Gmail keeps its rule of never replaying on its own.
6. **Read, star, Starred, Retry and read state are shown by capability, not by mode name.** `AccountStatus.capabilities.triageSurfaces` states it explicitly (a synthetic session sets it; Gmail leaves the field absent and clients keep their previous behaviour). The seeded Inbox is a realistic read/unread mix: the user's own messages are read, conversations whose newest message the user wrote are read (`conv-02`, `conv-04`, `conv-14`, `conv-16`), a few others are read (`conv-03`, `conv-10`), the two initially archived conversations are read, and the remaining 10 of the 16 Inbox conversations are unread.
7. **The one-time reset is disclosed on a startup gate** backed by two new IPC commands (status and accept). Backup, reset and the failure paths are described in the stage 4 plan and implemented with the transition state machine.
8. **Reminders** keep the Gmail local rules; copy for the retired archive/restore phases and any fixture text that became untrue is updated. Provider-flavoured error copy does not appear for fixture operations.

Unchanged by these decisions: wire mode stays `fixture`, the account stays `fixture-account`, no OAuth, no Keychain, no HTTP client, cached-only search, all 18 conversations present (including the two initially archived `conv-06` and `conv-15`), and the fake pause/reject environment controls apply only to synthetic writes and never reach the live provider.

## Question and recommendation

Investigate replacing the native fixture store/worker with `GmailCore` and a built-in, credential-free `SyntheticProvider`. This is a decision spike, not authorization to change production behavior. Baseline: `58e0bc7`.

**Recommendation: GO for staged unification; NO-GO for an unmodified provider-only substitution.** GmailCore already accepts `Arc<dyn GmailReadProvider>` and an injected clock. The provider must own durable synthetic provider facts; the core needs a small explicit fixture policy for mode/capabilities/lifecycle and reminders. Keeping a second operation ledger is avoidable, but silently changing the fixture contract is not acceptable. After those gates, delete the fixture `Store`, worker, reminder implementation and `MailCore` facade, and hold one `GmailCore` in shell state with a session policy instead of the `Backend` enum. Move the 18-conversation data out of `seed.rs` into the synthetic module before deleting that file. Retain shared `CancelToken` infrastructure currently located in `provider.rs`; removing the old archive fake must not remove Gmail cancellation support.

## Evidence checkpoints

- Required architecture, status, development and ADR 0001 read. Current docs explicitly promise a separate durable native fixture profile, seed-once behavior, archive-only mailbox actions, local drafts and synthetic attachment transfers.
- `gmail/sync.rs::open_with_clock` has no direct OAuth/Keychain dependency: those belong to the injected production `GmailProvider`. Startup currently interprets `has_credentials()` as a restore signal; a synthetic implementation needs an explicit local-ready policy rather than inventing real credentials.
- `gmail/sync.rs::account_status` hardcodes `MailMode::Gmail`; `mutation_access()` is a Boolean grant covering archive/read/star. Neither preserves fixture wire behavior by itself.
- All requested fixture test files were inventoried by test function name (appendix below). No production files are changed by this spike.

## Implementation stages (each must remain green and shippable)

1. Port fixture-specific guarantees to tests against GmailCore, retain both existing backends, and add a production synthetic data/provider module independent of test support. Keep the default fixture path unchanged.
2. Introduce explicit internal session policy in GmailCore: fixture identity/status, archive-only admission, unsupported errors, cached-only search, local readiness and non-destructive lifecycle. Implement persistent synthetic provider facts and seed-once discovery including the two initially archived conversations. Keep Gmail policy unchanged.
3. Resolve reminder behavior explicitly and cover it with acceptance/race/restart tests; move synthetic attachments/reply metadata behind provider/core seams. Preserve local drafts and fixture profile safety. Add opt-in synthetic-core launch path for validation.
4. Switch fixture default only after all mapped guarantees pass and profile transition disclosure is implemented. Keep the old database as backup. Remove the legacy backend after parity validation; update current docs and browser contract tests. Coordinating thread owns end-to-end validation and merge sequencing.

## Risks and decision gates

A fresh provider seeded into memory on every launch can overwrite archived provider facts at the next sync. Gmail discovery only lists Inbox, so it cannot by itself reproduce the two archived seed threads. GmailCore may expose read/star or destructive disconnect if fixture mode is represented as Gmail. Reminder scheduling currently has different mailbox effects. These are design gates for implementation, not bugs established by this spike.

The prototype will be published separately at [maintenance/p4-synthetic-provider-prototype](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/tree/maintenance/p4-synthetic-provider-prototype), marked throwaway and not for merge. This PR contains only this ADR.

## Behavior inventory and required policy

References are repository-relative; function names identify the reviewed seam. **Blocker** means an unmodified provider-only substitution cannot preserve the contract. It does not mean the staged implementation is infeasible.

| Surface | Fixture today / GmailCore with synthetic provider | Classification and implementation condition |
|---|---|---|
| Account/status | `src-tauri/src/main.rs::Backend::account_status` returns fixture/Connected/Idle, no mutation grant, 18 cached, complete, no timestamp, limit 0. `gmail/sync.rs::account_status` returns Gmail, observed grant, transient Authenticating/Syncing, timestamps and limit 100. | **Blocker** to drop-in. Internal fixture policy must retain fixture mode/identity/capability presentation; disclose initial loading if asynchronous bootstrap is retained. Do not masquerade as a connected Google account. |
| Credentials | Fixture never opens OAuth or Keychain. GmailCore only calls provider methods; shell constructs GmailProvider/Keychain only in Gmail branch. `gmail/types.rs::GmailReadProvider` does not require a secret type. | **Same** possible. Synthetic provider is constructed directly, with no HTTP client or Secrets. Explicit local-ready startup should replace the misleading credential-presence signal in production. |
| Lifecycle | Fixture rejects connect/disconnect/upgrade/sync commands with `InvalidRequest { field: "mode" }`. Gmail disconnect cancels work and clears account/cache. | **Blocker** without fixture admission policy. Preserve errors and prevent synthetic disconnect from erasing local state. |
| Mailbox gates | Fixture archives/restores, rejects read/star singles/groups with `ReadOnly`; some other unsupported commands use mode errors. GmailCore's Boolean mutation grant admits all three dimensions (`accept_action`, `accept_operation`). | **Blocker**. Per-session archive-only gate is required at core admission, not only hidden controls. Retain existing error variants initially; consistency is a separate contract change. |
| Fake controls | `provider.rs::FakeArchiveProvider::from_env`: paused blocks writes cancellation-aware; reject rejects the next write once; success/default succeeds. | **Different-but-acceptable** implementation: preserve exact environment semantics only in SyntheticProvider writes, leaving reads/bootstrap responsive. Never route the variable to GmailProvider. |
| Seed/restart | `store.rs::migrate_and_seed` transaction seeds `conv-01`…`conv-18` once, including archived `conv-06`/`conv-15`; restarts retain facts/history. Gmail discovery fetches Inbox and does not seed archived rows. | **Blocker** without durable synthetic provider state and initial all-seed cache import. A one-time synthetic bootstrap must preserve actual Inbox facts. Existing `GmailCore::load_search_conversation` / `GmailStore::save_search` can preload the two archived seeds explicitly without pretending they are Inbox mail. Ordinary discovery/history intentionally excludes uncached archived bodies (`history_does_not_import_new_archived_thread_bodies_into_the_bounded_cache`). Reopening an in-memory default provider is insufficient. |
| Undo/clock | `clock.rs`, both stores and both `open_with_clock` facades use 10 seconds and persisted acceptance/preimages; undo may cancel queued work or enqueue compensation. | **Same** core guarantee. Use injected Clock for deadlines; worker Condvar/Instant scheduling still needs bounded waits/notifications. Preserve strict boundary, immutable targets, partial groups, restart and supersession tests. |
| Reminders | `store/reminders.rs::put_reminder` stages archive, worker reconciles removing/pending/returning states and restores prior membership. GmailStore reminders hide locally, do not write provider; no-reply requires connected fresh complete thread read plus account/generation/revision fences (`gmail/sync.rs`, `gmail/store.rs`, UX-11). | **Blocker** to exact parity. Recommended explicit product adjustment: synthetic mode adopts Gmail's local reminder rules, with no Google I/O and fresh reads from the durable synthetic provider. Update fixture disclosures and tests; archive/restore failure-phase tests become obsolete only for that approved adjustment. Do not claim a prototype reminder proves legacy parity. |
| Search | `lib.rs::search_mail` / `store.rs::search_mail` evaluate cached fixture data. Gmail `search_mail` can progressively scan provider candidates with bounded incomplete coverage. | **Same** if fixture policy forces cached-only semantics and all 18 are cached; do not silently enable Gmail discovery/search controls. |

# Current architecture

**Scope:** This is an inventory of architecture that exists in the source tree. It describes code paths and ownership. For feature availability and validation results, see [current status](current-status.md). For the selected first-build scope, see [ADR 0001](adr/0001-single-account-desktop-email-client.md). [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) is a historical proposal; its design recommendations are not evidence of implementation.

## Runtime and boundaries

The app has a Vue/TypeScript frontend, a Tauri 2 shell, and the Rust `mail-core` crate. The Rust crate owns persistence and provider operations. The frontend talks through a `MailClient` interface. In native mode, `createTauriMailClient` maps that interface to named Tauri commands. In browser mode, `browser-fake.ts` supplies a synthetic in-memory client. The shared interface and generated wire types are in [client.ts](../src/lib/ipc/client.ts), [tauri-client.ts](../src/lib/ipc/tauri-client.ts), [browser-fake.ts](../src/lib/ipc/browser-fake.ts), and [generated.ts](../src/lib/ipc/generated.ts). Rust DTOs are the source for generated TypeScript; `crates/mail-core/src/bin/generate-types.rs` generates the file.

The shared Tauri entry point in [lib.rs](../src-tauri/src/lib.rs) holds the module list and the command handler list. [setup.rs](../src-tauri/src/setup.rs) selects fixture or Gmail mode on desktop, opens the corresponding Rust core (fixture mode is the Gmail core on the built-in synthetic provider, ADR 0002) and handles window and run events; [state.rs](../src-tauri/src/state.rs) holds the single `GmailCore`, the draft service, the attachment transfer registry and the close gate; the commands under [commands/](../src-tauri/src/commands) translate IPC to core calls and emit mailbox/draft/close events. Mail rules live in `mail-core`, not the shell. Desktop [main.rs](../src-tauri/src/main.rs) is a thin launcher. Android forces fixture mode and does not run the desktop close/exit gate. A pre-existing legacy fixture database is retired once by [fixture_transition.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/fixture_transition.rs), behind a startup screen (`StartupRoot.vue`, two IPC commands). Android's generated Gradle project is under `src-tauri/gen/android`; setup and build steps are in [development guide](development.md). The webview does not access SQLite or provider HTTP directly. Its capabilities and generated command permissions are under [src-tauri/capabilities](../src-tauri/capabilities/main-window.json) and [src-tauri/permissions/autogenerated](../src-tauri/permissions/autogenerated).

## Rust state and transaction ownership

There is one mail core. `GmailCore` ([gmail/sync.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/sync.rs)) serves two kinds of session, distinguished by an explicit `SessionPolicy` ([gmail/session.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/session.rs)): a Gmail session over the live provider, and a synthetic (fixture) session over `SyntheticGmailProvider` ([synthetic/](../crates/mail-core/src/synthetic)), whose 18 conversations and per-message INBOX/UNREAD/STARRED facts live in a transactional, seed-once `synthetic-provider.db`. The policy decides identity and status, admission, lifecycle rejections, cached-only search, local readiness and restart behaviour (interrupted unlanded writes are requeued for a synthetic session and never auto-replayed for Gmail). Command acceptance returns receipts after persistence; provider work is performed by a worker outside the acceptance transaction. Worker recovery and undo state are durable.

The Gmail session is implemented in [gmail/sync.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/sync.rs), [gmail/store.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/store.rs), [gmail/operations.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/operations.rs), and the Gmail provider modules. The sync service owns the Gmail cache and coordinates provider reads and queued operations. SQLite transactions persist local state; network calls occur through the provider path. [gmail/provider.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/provider.rs) owns HTTP, credentials, pacing, status, and quota handling; [gmail/provider/api.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/provider/api.rs) implements the `GmailProvider` trait (auth/session, reads and writes; defined in [gmail/types.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/types.rs)) for the concrete `LiveGmailProvider`; [gmail/parse.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/parse.rs) contains pure Gmail response and message parsing. OAuth flow, token access, and secret storage are in [gmail/auth.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/auth.rs) and [gmail/secrets.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/secrets.rs). The service exposes account status and sync state through DTOs. Runtime success on a supported macOS installation is a separate validation question; see [current status](current-status.md).

Gmail schema upgrades are owned by `gmail/store_schema.rs`. The authoritative
`meta.schema_version` advances through `gmail-migrations-1` to
`gmail-migrations-9`, with each stage's DDL, backfills and marker in one
transaction. Pre-numbered `gmail-1` and `gmail-2` profiles had ambiguous physical
layouts, so only those historical migration bodies inspect optional columns.
An already-current profile performs no migration writes. Fresh profiles use the
canonical schema captured from the pre-change store. Unknown or newer markers
fail before schema changes. Startup crash recovery runs explicitly after
migration: globally applying operations become uncertain and lose `last_error`.
Reconnect recovery remains account-scoped and additionally clears `failure`;
these distinct semantics are preserved.

`GmailStore` stays one type owning the single SQLite connection; its impl and
helpers are split by responsibility under `gmail/store/`. `store.rs` holds the
shared types and the struct; every method that opens a transaction still opens
exactly one, so acceptance and reconciliation keep their atomic scope.

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `profile` | open and startup recovery, account identity, generation, sync checkpoints, disconnect cleanup, saved split |
| `cache`, `cache_rows` | cached conversation reads; thread and fact upserts, eviction, conversation building, `meta` helpers |
| `ingestion` | discovery and history pages, rediscovery |
| `search`, `search_support` | cached search, done, trash and starred lists; search admission and eviction |
| `acceptance`, `operation_rows` | single-operation acceptance and retry; acceptance transaction, preimages, operation row codecs |
| `worker` | claim, confirm, reconcile, defer, requeue and finish; a definitely rejected write fails on its own and the pass moves on to the next queued write, while transient and account-wide errors requeue it and back off |
| `undo`, `undo_support` | single-operation undo and its compensation helpers |
| `group_acceptance`, `group_queries`, `group_undo`, `group_rows` | group acceptance, status queries, group undo and the shared group row helpers |
| `activity` | effective conversation state and the activity list |
| `reminders`, `destinations` | local reminders; destination snapshots |

Store tests live in `gmail/store_tests.rs` beside `migration_tests.rs`.

Storage failures are diagnosable without leaking data. Every storage failure
still reaches the wire as `MailError::StorageUnavailable`, unchanged, but the
point that produced it first logs exactly one line through the `log` facade:
the call site's `file:line`, a static cause tag (`sqlite`, `lock_poisoned`,
`thread_join`, `path_unavailable`, `missing_persisted_row` and similar) and,
for SQLite errors, the primary result code name and extended code. The line
is built only from static strings and numbers; the Display text of the
underlying error is never read, because SQLite messages can quote values and
SQL. `mail-core` owns the helper in [storage_log.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/storage_log.rs);
the shell has its own small helper and the stderr logger in
[diagnostics.rs](../src-tauri/src/diagnostics.rs), which passes only the two
storage log targets and drops everything else. Re-mapping an error that was
already a `MailError` does not log a second time. Rejections because the sync
worker is stopped or halted are not logged: the failure that halted it already was.

Drafts are stored in a separate `<selected-profile>/local-drafts` SQLite database by [drafts/store.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/drafts/store.rs), with revision and account identity types in [drafts/types.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/drafts/types.rs). The store uses WAL and FULL synchronous mode. Saves and deletes are revision-checked and return receipts after commit; deletion records request tombstones so a late save cannot recreate a removed draft. The frontend draft composable and editor coordinate local edits, acknowledged saves, and error recovery in [useDrafts.ts](../src/composables/useDrafts.ts), [DraftEditorCore.vue](../src/components/DraftEditorCore.vue), and [ReplyComposer.vue](../src/components/ReplyComposer.vue). Drafts remain local to the profile and do not sync to Gmail. Which account a draft belongs to, reply revalidation against the displayed conversation, and the session epoch that rejects a reply prepared across a connect or disconnect are decided by `DraftService` in [drafts/service.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/drafts/service.rs); the shell commands only delegate to it.

The native close path uses a request/acknowledgement gate in [close_gate.rs](../src-tauri/src/close_gate.rs). The shell asks the frontend to flush and close dirty draft state; the frontend acknowledges only after the latest save is committed, and cancels close when save fails. Frontend coordination lives in [App.vue](../src/App.vue) and the draft composable. The governing contract is [vertical slice 04](vertical-slice-04.md).

## Frontend coordination

[App.vue](../src/App.vue) is the composition root for navigation, focused conversation, panels, and mailbox actions. [useMailbox.ts](../src/composables/useMailbox.ts) owns account-scoped focus and mailbox query coordination and keeps the public `Mailbox` shape. It composes focused modules that receive their dependencies as arguments rather than closing over the parent: [useMailboxSelection.ts](../src/composables/useMailboxSelection.ts) owns the UX-05 selection set, range anchor and `SELECTION_MAX` bound (the parent clears it on context, account and saved-view invalidation and prunes it after each authoritative list read), [useMailboxGroups.ts](../src/composables/useMailboxGroups.ts) owns UX-05 group dispatch, the single group notice, lost-response recovery on the original request id, partial group Undo, restart notice rehydration and the Activity group history/detail reads, [useMailboxDetailCache.ts](../src/composables/useMailboxDetailCache.ts) owns the bounded neighbor-detail cache, its TTL, the single-slot prefetch and the J/K reader loading delay (its fence is an epoch the owner bumps through `invalidateDetailCache()` on every refresh, mutation start, reader close, account change and disconnect), [useMailboxAccount.ts](../src/composables/useMailboxAccount.ts) owns authoritative account/mode status and the connect, disconnect, sync, enable-actions and cancel-upgrade lifecycle (each status read is fenced by its own request token and the session; it reports an account-identity change and a confirmed disconnect to `useMailbox` through callbacks, and `useMailbox` resets list, reader, group and selection state and bumps the session generation inside them), and [mailbox-refs.ts](../src/composables/mailbox-refs.ts) and [mailbox-session.ts](../src/composables/mailbox-session.ts) hold the shared conversation-reference helpers and the session/command-fence types. Session invalidation is an explicit argument: `useMailbox` owns the session counters and hands extracted pieces a read-only `MailboxSession` (generation and detached flag) plus the shared command fence; each async path captures the generation before its first await and drops its result when it moved. Components render the inbox, reader, composer, activity, and account controls. The client subscription events are invalidation hints; the frontend reloads through client queries.

The shell passes explicit dependencies to its extracted surface state: [useGoChord.ts](../src/composables/useGoChord.ts) handles the G-chord timer, [useActionNotice.ts](../src/composables/useActionNotice.ts) derives the action notice and Undo window, [useAccountNotes.ts](../src/composables/useAccountNotes.ts) derives account and empty-line facts, [useContactContext.ts](../src/composables/useContactContext.ts) derives contact identities and pane visibility, [useSearchSurface.ts](../src/composables/useSearchSurface.ts) owns search entry, suggestions and recent queries, [useViewportContact.ts](../src/composables/useViewportContact.ts) owns the contact disclosure, the 1000px media query and the focus handoff when it is crossed, and [useAttachmentChooser.ts](../src/composables/useAttachmentChooser.ts) owns the chooser's snapshot and the origin and scroll it returns to. The shell retains navigation and passes its epoch accessors to search so newer navigation supersedes a pending search. [error-text.ts](../src/lib/error-text.ts) formats errors shown by the shell. There is no line-count target for `App.vue`: the earlier 1,800-line target was retired by the owner's decision, because what remains in the shell is mostly reader navigation and focus restoration (the Undo focus race fix lives there and its timing is thinly tested), which is left in place deliberately rather than moved for a number.

The production native client and browser fake share the same `MailClient` contract, but they do not share persistence or provider behavior. What is guaranteed to agree is the operation-ledger contract: shared scenario files in [tests/fixtures/contract-scenarios](../tests/fixtures/contract-scenarios) (acceptance, idempotent replay, undo, groups, typed errors) are executed by [contract_scenarios.rs](../crates/mail-core/tests/contract_scenarios.rs) against both Rust profiles (`GmailCore` with the shared fake provider, and a synthetic session on the built-in provider) and by [contract-scenarios.test.ts](../tests/browser-fake/contract-scenarios.test.ts) against the browser fake, with each side's own fake clock. Any divergence is named in the runners' `KNOWN_DIVERGENCES` tables and is still executed (it must fail), so it stays visible; the tables are empty today. Anything the scenarios do not cover (read models other than Inbox and Activity, search, drafts, reminders, durability across restart) is not covered by this guarantee. Format and how to add a scenario: [development guidance](development.md#contract-scenarios). Browser tests and preview use the fake client; they cannot establish native SQLite, OAuth, OS keychain, system dialogs, or WKWebView behavior. The boundary and runtime checks are recorded in [development guidance](development.md) and [current status](current-status.md).

## Validation task boundaries

The `mise run check` task serially runs headless core tests, the generated IPC contract check, core formatting and clippy, frontend tests, and frontend typechecking. It does not require GTK/WebKit development packages. Native shell clippy, bridge tests, and the web production build are separate tasks; `mise run check:all` runs the full sequence, including `lint:native`, serially after native prerequisites are installed. CI installs Linux prerequisites before running this full gate. Rendered Chromium suites remain opt-in and are not part of CI.

# ADR 0001: Start with a single-account desktop email client

**Status:** Accepted — first-build direction and scope; not authorization to connect a mailbox or send mail.

## Context

Email OS's long-term direction is a composable email client whose views, signals, commands, and workflows can be adapted by users and agents. The [PRD](../../PRD.md) describes that destination, not a suitably narrow first build.

The immediate goal is a limited replacement for Superhuman. The user has confirmed that **one account on desktop is a good starting point**. The first build should therefore replace a complete everyday activity, rather than demonstrate a platform or add another tool alongside the existing client.

[Experiment 1](../../EXPERIMENT-01.md) proposes a read-only, teachable reply queue. That remains a possible later customization study, but handing users back to another client to reply would not validate the immediate replacement goal.

At the time of this ADR, the repository contained planning and static reviews. The narrower Slice 01 fixture baseline and Slice 02 read-only Gmail path are now implemented; see the slice contracts for their boundaries and `docs/development.md` for validation status. This ADR's broader provider-backed composition, sending, Gmail archive/read-state actions, search, and saved-view scope remains future work; macOS Slice 02 runtime validation is still pending.

## Decision

Build a **keyboard-first, single-account desktop client for a complete inbox-processing session**, with one small configurable-view capability.

The initial promise is:

> I can open Email OS, process my inbox, and finish ordinary replies without switching to Superhuman.

The primary loop is:

```text
Open inbox → navigate → read conversation → reply or archive → next
```

Optimize this loop for speed, predictable interaction, and trustworthy state before adding intelligent prioritization or general extensibility.

### Initial boundaries

- One connected account, not a unified multi-account inbox.
- One desktop operating system for the first developer build. macOS is approved for the Slice 02 pilot; the broader platform/runtime gate remains pending.
- Gmail REST is approved for the narrow, read-only disposable-account Slice 02 pilot. This does not authorize write scopes or broader provider capabilities; do not build a second provider merely to demonstrate abstraction.
- No custom Android surface in this build. An existing provider client remains the mobile fallback; this sequencing does not remove Android from the product vision.
- Manual operation must work without AI or external inference.
- Initial validation is personal dogfooding, not a recruited multi-user pilot.

## First-build scope

### 1. Inbox and reading

- Inbox list and conversation reader with enough message history to reply confidently.
- Predictable keyboard navigation, focus, and shortcuts for next/previous, open/back, reply, archive, and read/unread.
- Safe message rendering. A plain-text presentation is acceptable initially; HTML fidelity is not a reason to weaken isolation or sanitization.
- Visible loading, freshness, incomplete-context, and synchronization-error states.
- An explicit fallback to the provider client for unsupported operations or message formats.

### 2. Composition and sending

- Reply, reply-all, and simple new-message composition.
- Clearly displayed recipients, distinguishing reply from reply-all; no hidden recipient expansion.
- Draft persistence across application restart, including recipient and body edits.
- Basic file attachment upload/download, with explicit size/type limitations and failures. Inline editing, attachment previews, and sophisticated formatting are deferred.
- Explicit user-initiated sending, with visible operation status and failure recovery.

Drafts may initially be application-local. The interface must make that limitation clear: cross-device/provider draft synchronization is not promised.

### 3. Mailbox actions and search

- Archive and read/unread changes reflected in provider state, so ordinary mailbox state remains consistent with other clients.
- Immediate local feedback backed by durable staging and reconciliation, not optimistic success messages that hide failures.
- Basic search sufficient to find an older conversation. Provider-backed search is acceptable; a complete local full-text index is not required.
- Search results must disclose whether they cover the provider mailbox or only cached data.

### UX-08 bounded star decision

UX-08 explicitly adds observed per-message STARRED facts and narrow Star/Unstar
setters over the immutable inventory observed at acceptance. This is a bounded
addition to the original archive/read action set, not arbitrary label authority:
INBOX and UNREAD remain independent, and the existing durable groups, preimages,
Undo and uncertain-outcome reconciliation are reused. Legacy/partial facts stay
unknown. Cached Starred includes archived/recovery mail but never promises
provider-complete coverage. No new OAuth scope is requested; actual writes still
require the verified modify grant, explicit user action and operator-approved
disposable-account validation. The legacy archive-only fixture profile does not
gain star controls. Native macOS/provider convergence remains a separate gate.
Saved splits/search are not prerequisites and are not reimplemented here.

### UX-09 bounded destination decision

UX-09 increment A explicitly permits read-only Gmail destination metadata and
bounded provider pages for Sent, provider Drafts, All Mail (excluding Spam/Trash),
Spam, Trash and existing user labels. Rationale: the 100-conversation inbox cache
cannot honestly serve those destinations. Separate timestamped SQLite snapshots
must not change inbox/history checkpoints or evict durable-operation recovery.
Provider Drafts remain read-only and distinct from application-local drafts.
This does not authorize Trash/Spam writes, sending, label create/delete, arbitrary
system-label mutation, or a second provider. Label/Move remain unavailable until
a separate durable logical-intent/recovery increment satisfies the UX-09 contract.
The Gmail readonly scope suffices for increment A; all existing real-account
and native validation gates remain. No new mailbox access is authorized here.

### 4. One configurable view

Provide one additional saved queue defined by a bounded, declarative filter over sender, domain, or existing provider labels, with a stable default order. It must reuse the ordinary reader, composer, and mailbox commands.

- A small manual editor is sufficient; no natural-language authoring is required.
- Keep the full inbox accessible. Filtering must not silently archive, relabel, or hide mail from the provider inbox.
- Store the definition locally for the first build; do not imply it follows the user to mobile.
- If referenced data is not loaded, disclose the view's coverage.

This is a small test of the composable direction, not a general rules engine. Do not add new provider permissions or mutation capabilities merely to support view configuration.

### UX-10 bounded triage decision

[UX-10 A](../ux-10-bounded-triage.md) adds read-only **known cached Trash**
browsing and observed per-message TRASH/SPAM facts. This is an explicit narrow
extension of browsing, not a complete UX-09 folder catalog or broader mutation
authority. Current observed Trash/Spam excludes a conversation from local Done
even when it has old archive evidence. Legacy absence remains unknown.

Trash/recover writes and their Undo remain deferred: archive is not trash, and
the current archive/read preimages cannot restore a multi-dimension trash side
effect. The recovery destination decision is recorded in the UX-10 contract.
Mute requires actual future-message semantics, not INBOX removal; Spam/recover
needs validated provider effects. Important/Other requires independent local view
membership and explicit scope. Sender/domain rules, Block and Unsubscribe remain
deferred pending separate bounded execution/authority contracts. No send,
arbitrary URL opener, permanent deletion or empty-Trash is introduced.

## Architecture constraints

Preserve a few internal boundaries without committing to a public SDK:

1. **Mail integration and local state:** own credentials, synchronization, message identity, caching, and reconciliation outside UI components.
2. **Views:** select and order conversations from available data; they do not execute mailbox mutations.
3. **Commands and execution:** route UI actions through one typed boundary responsible for validation, durable operation state, concurrency, and recovery.
4. **Presentation:** consume those interfaces for the default inbox and the configurable view.

Use local data for responsive navigation where available. Opening a cached conversation must not require a fresh provider request to render its cached content.

Persist drafts and staged operations across restart. Cached reading and draft editing should remain usable without a connection; full offline mailbox coverage and offline search completeness are not required. Distinguish local, pending, and provider-confirmed state.

A send with an ambiguous remote outcome must enter an explicit **outcome unknown** state and be reconciled rather than blindly retried. Do not promise universal exactly-once sending or provider-side undo after delivery.

Synchronization is required while the application is running. Guaranteed synchronization, sending, or timer execution while the application is fully quit is out of scope. Hide-versus-quit behavior must be documented.

Framework, storage implementation, shell, and reuse strategy require separate technical decisions. This ADR does not select Tauri, Electron, Rust, React, or either reviewed fork.

## Safety and release gates

Narrow scope does not justify weaker mail integrity or privacy.

Before primary-mailbox dogfooding, use synthetic fixtures and a disposable account to validate:

- Authentication refresh/revocation and secure credential storage.
- Hostile-message rendering, blocked active content, and bloc

# ADR 0002: Fixture mode as a synthetic provider

**Status:** Implemented (stages 1–4). Stage 4 landed with the owner's decisions below: the default switched to the synthetic core, the legacy `MailCore` backend, its store and worker and the `EMAIL_OS_SYNTHETIC_CORE` opt-in were removed, and the one-time transition is the `fixture_transition` state machine behind the startup gate. The sections below are the original investigation and are kept as the record of why.

## Decisions

Taken on 2026-11-14 on the coordinating thread's recommendation, after the project owner asked for the remaining maintenance tickets to run. They authorise **stages 1 to 3** only. The owner can still redirect before stage 4 (switching the default and deleting the legacy backend); nothing below is a user-facing change until then.

1. **Staged unification**, as recommended above. The legacy `MailCore` backend stays the default and is not touched until stage 4.
2. **The unified fixture gains read and star.** Synthetic fixture mode admits archive, read and star (single and group), and the cached Starred list works. This departs from the "archive-only" wording in the stages and inventory below, which was about preserving today's errors. Cached Trash and provider destinations stay rejected with today's error variants. Connect, disconnect, permission upgrade and manual sync stay rejected with `InvalidRequest { field: "mode" }`, and nothing in synthetic mode may erase local state the way a Gmail disconnect does.
3. **Synthetic reminders follow the Gmail core's local rules** (hide locally, no provider write). The legacy fixture's archive/restore reminder phases are retired when stage 4 lands, not before.
4. **The on-disk transition (stage 4) is a one-time reset with disclosure and a retained backup**, local drafts untouched. It is planned, not implemented, in stages 1–3.

### Stage 4 decisions (owner, 2026-11-15)

5. **Interrupted writes are requeued by the synthetic policy.** A write interrupted before the provider recorded it is reconciled against the provider's durable facts at startup: landed means confirmed, unlanded means requeued and applied again. This matches the legacy fixture and is a session-policy method (`replay_unlanded_interrupted_writes`), not a mode check. Gmail keeps its rule of never replaying on its own.
6. **Read, star, Starred, Retry and read state are shown by capability, not by mode name.** `AccountStatus.capabilities.triageSurfaces` states it explicitly (a synthetic session sets it; Gmail leaves the field absent and clients keep their previous behaviour). The seeded Inbox is a realistic read/unread mix: the user's own messages are read, conversations whose newest message the user wrote are read (`conv-02`, `conv-04`, `conv-14`, `conv-16`), a few others are read (`conv-03`, `conv-10`), the two initially archived conversations are read, and the remaining 10 of the 16 Inbox conversations are unread.
7. **The one-time reset is disclosed on a startup gate** backed by two new IPC commands (status and accept). Backup, reset and the failure paths are described in the stage 4 plan and implemented with the transition state machine.
8. **Reminders** keep the Gmail local rules; copy for the retired archive/restore phases and any fixture text that became untrue is updated. Provider-flavoured error copy does not appear for fixture operations.

Unchanged by these decisions: wire mode stays `fixture`, the account stays `fixture-account`, no OAuth, no Keychain, no HTTP client, cached-only search, all 18 conversations present (including the two initially archived `conv-06` and `conv-15`), and the fake pause/reject environment controls apply only to synthetic writes and never reach the live provider.

## Question and recommendation

Investigate replacing the native fixture store/worker with `GmailCore` and a built-in, credential-free `SyntheticProvider`. This is a decision spike, not authorization to change production behavior. Baseline: `58e0bc7`.

**Recommendation: GO for staged unification; NO-GO for an unmodified provider-only substitution.** GmailCore already accepts `Arc<dyn GmailReadProvider>` and an injected clock. The provider must own durable synthetic provider facts; the core needs a small explicit fixture policy for mode/capabilities/lifecycle and reminders. Keeping a second operation ledger is avoidable, but silently changing the fixture contract is not acceptable. After those gates, delete the fixture `Store`, worker, reminder implementation and `MailCore` facade, and hold one `GmailCore` in shell state with a session policy instead of the `Backend` enum. Move the 18-conversation data out of `seed.rs` into the synthetic module before deleting that file. Retain shared `CancelToken` infrastructure currently located in `provider.rs`; removing the old archive fake must not remove Gmail cancellation support.

## Evidence checkpoints

- Required architecture, status, development and ADR 0001 read. Current docs explicitly promise a separate durable native fixture profile, seed-once behavior, archive-only mailbox actions, local drafts and synthetic attachment transfers.
- `gmail/sync.rs::open_with_clock` has no direct OAuth/Keychain dependency: those belong to the injected production `GmailProvider`. Startup currently interprets `has_credentials()` as a restore signal; a synthetic implementation needs an explicit local-ready policy rather than inventing real credentials.
- `gmail/sync.rs::account_status` hardcodes `MailMode::Gmail`; `mutation_access()` is a Boolean grant covering archive/read/star. Neither preserves fixture wire behavior by itself.
- All requested fixture test files were inventoried by test function name (appendix below). No production files are changed by this spike.

## Implementation stages (each must remain green and shippable)

1. Port fixture-specific guarantees to tests against GmailCore, retain both existing backends, and add a production synthetic data/provider module independent of test support. Keep the default fixture path unchanged.
2. Introduce explicit internal session policy in GmailCore: fixture identity/status, archive-only admission, unsupported errors, cached-only search, local readiness and non-destructive lifecycle. Implement persistent synthetic provider facts and seed-once discovery including the two initially archived conversations. Keep Gmail policy unchanged.
3. Resolve reminder behavior explicitly and cover it with acceptance/race/restart tests; move synthetic attachments/reply metadata behind provider/core seams. Preserve local drafts and fixture profile safety. Add opt-in synthetic-core launch path for validation.
4. Switch fixture default only after all mapped guarantees pass and profile transition disclosure is implemented. Keep the old database as backup. Remove the legacy backend after parity validation; update current docs and browser contract tests. Coordinating thread owns end-to-end validation and merge sequencing.

## Risks and decision gates

A fresh provider seeded into memory on every launch can overwrite archived provider facts at the next sync. Gmail discovery only lists Inbox, so it cannot by itself reproduce the two archived seed threads. GmailCore may expose read/star or destructive disconnect if fixture mode is represented as Gmail. Reminder scheduling currently has different mailbox effects. These are design gates for implementation, not bugs established by this spike.

The prototype will be published separately at [maintenance/p4-synthetic-provider-prototype](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/tree/maintenance/p4-synthetic-provider-prototype), marked throwaway and not for merge. This PR contains only this ADR.

Opening that new file beside `mail.db` is not a migration. `docs/development.md` promises seeds never reset provider facts or operation history; `docs/current-status.md` promises durable synthetic state and drafts. A silent reset violates that promise.

Reminder policy work may exceed this. Net production reduction is plausibly 1,000–2,000 lines, contingent on review. # ADR 0002: Fixture mode as a synthetic provider

**Status:** Implemented (stages 1–4). Stage 4 landed with the owner's decisions below: the default switched to the synthetic core, the legacy `MailCore` backend, its store and worker and the `EMAIL_OS_SYNTHETIC_CORE` opt-in were removed, and the one-time transition is the `fixture_transition` state machine behind the startup gate. The sections below are the original investigation and are kept as the record of why.

## Decisions

Taken on 2026-11-14 on the coordinating thread's recommendation, after the project owner asked for the remaining maintenance tickets to run. They authorise **stages 1 to 3** only. The owner can still redirect before stage 4 (switching the default and deleting the legacy backend); nothing below is a user-facing change until then.

1. **Staged unification**, as recommended above. The legacy `MailCore` backend stays the default and is not touched until stage 4.
2. **The unified fixture gains read and star.** Synthetic fixture mode admits archive, read and star (single and group), and the cached Starred list works. This departs from the "archive-only" wording in the stages and inventory below, which was about preserving today's errors. Cached Trash and provider destinations stay rejected with today's error variants. Connect, disconnect, permission upgrade and manual sync stay rejected with `InvalidRequest { field: "mode" }`, and nothing in synthetic mode may erase local state the way a Gmail disconnect does.
3. **Synthetic reminders follow the Gmail core's local rules** (hide locally, no provider write). The legacy fixture's archive/restore reminder phases are retired when stage 4 lands, not before.
4. **The on-disk transition (stage 4) is a one-time reset with disclosure and a retained backup**, local drafts untouched. It is planned, not implemented, in stages 1–3.

### Stage 4 decisions (owner, 2026-11-15)

5. **Interrupted writes are requeued by the synthetic policy.** A write interrupted before the provider recorded it is reconciled against the provider's durable facts at startup: landed means confirmed, unlanded means requeued and applied again. This matches the legacy fixture and is a session-policy method (`replay_unlanded_interrupted_writes`), not a mode check. Gmail keeps its rule of never replaying on its own.
6. **Read, star, Starred, Retry and read state are shown by capability, not by mode name.** `AccountStatus.capabilities.triageSurfaces` states it explicitly (a synthetic session sets it; Gmail leaves the field absent and clients keep their previous behaviour). The seeded Inbox is a realistic read/unread mix: the user's own messages are read, conversations whose newest message the user wrote are read (`conv-02`, `conv-04`, `conv-14`, `conv-16`), a few others are read (`conv-03`, `conv-10`), the two initially archived conversations are read, and the remaining 10 of the 16 Inbox conversations are unread.
7. **The one-time reset is disclosed on a startup gate** backed by two new IPC commands (status and accept). Backup, reset and the failure paths are described in the stage 4 plan and implemented with the transition state machine.
8. **Reminders** keep the Gmail local rules; copy for the retired archive/restore phases and any fixture text that became untrue is updated. Provider-flavoured error copy does not appear for fixture operations.

Unchanged by these decisions: wire mode stays `fixture`, the account stays `fixture-account`, no OAuth, no Keychain, no HTTP client, cached-only search, all 18 conversations present (including the two initially archived `conv-06` and `conv-15`), and the fake pause/reject environment controls apply only to synthetic writes and never reach the live provider.

## Question and recommendation

Investigate replacing the native fixture store/worker with `GmailCore` and a built-in, credential-free `SyntheticProvider`. This is a decision spike, not authorization to change production behavior. Baseline: `58e0bc7`.

**Recommendation: GO for staged unification; NO-GO for an unmodified provider-only substitution.** GmailCore already accepts `Arc<dyn GmailReadProvider>` and an injected clock. The provider must own durable synthetic provider facts; the core needs a small explicit fixture policy for mode/capabilities/lifecycle and reminders. Keeping a second operation ledger is avoidable, but silently changing the fixture contract is not acceptable. After those gates, delete the fixture `Store`, worker, reminder implementation and `MailCore` facade, and hold one `GmailCore` in shell state with a session policy instead of the `Backend` enum. Move the 18-conversation data out of `seed.rs` into the synthetic module before deleting that file. Retain shared `CancelToken` infrastructure currently located in `provider.rs`; removing the old archive fake must not remove Gmail cancellation support.

## Evidence checkpoints

- Required architecture, status, development and ADR 0001 read. Current docs explicitly promise a separate durable native fixture profile, seed-once behavior, archive-only mailbox actions, local drafts and synthetic attachment transfers.
- `gmail/sync.rs::open_with_clock` has no direct OAuth/Keychain dependency: those belong to the injected production `GmailProvider`. Startup currently interprets `has_credentials()` as a restore signal; a synthetic implementation needs an explicit local-ready policy rather than inventing real credentials.
- `gmail/sync.rs::account_status` hardcodes `MailMode::Gmail`; `mutation_access()` is a Boolean grant covering archive/read/star. Neither preserves fixture wire behavior by itself.
- All requested fixture test files were inventoried by test function name (appendix below). No production files are changed by this spike.
